As per the investigation by the police officials, on 18.11.2018, concerned police official reached the spot of accident and found one Honda City car no. DL-3CAK-0308 in accidental condition. That no eye witness was found. Later on, it was found that present injured Hamid Khan was admitted in ESI hospital and two other injured namely Rehan and Nizam were admitted in Appolo hospital, Sarita Vihar. Accordingly, initially FIR u/ 279, 337 IPC was recorded. Further, during investigation, it was found including on the statement of R-1/driver/accused that on 18.11.2018 he borrowed the offending vehicle from R-2 for attending a marriage. He was going in such marriage while driving such car in which his friends Rehan, Nazim, Akbar and Anas were also sitting. Further, on the way, they also made the present MACT No. 165/2020 Hamid Khan v. Yamin Page No 2 of 19 BK injured/claimant Hamid Khan sit in the car to show them the way. But, on the way, instead of brake, he pressed on the accelerator and a stray cow came on the way and in order to save the cow, the accident in question took place and his car struck against the wall. As a result, the car got damaged and people sitting therein received injuries. Further, during investigation, it was found that Rehan and Nazim received grievous injuries whereas injury to present claimant Hamid was dangerous as per the medical opinion. 4. Further, it was found that there was no third party insurance of such vehicle. 5. The police after investigation in present case filed charge sheet for offence u/s 279,338 IPC & 146/196 MV Act against the respondent no.1/driver. Present DAR was also filed by the investigating officer. 6. From the material on record, the following issues were framed on 25.09.2020 by my Ld. Predecessor: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 18.11.2019 involving vehicle bearing no.DL-3CAK-0308 being driven by R-1`and owned by R-2? 7. In this case, injured is minor of about 14 years age at the time of accident. 8. Mohd. Akbar Khan, father of minor injured Hamid Khan filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as MACT No. 165/2020 Hamid Khan v. Yamin Page No 3 of 19 BK Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents Ex. PW-1/1 to PW-1/5 (colly) including DAR, MLC of concerned hospital Master Hamid Khan(Minor) vs Yamin S/O Sh. Azad Hussain on 28 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174855318/ 2 and copy of Aadhar card. As per record, despite opportunity such witness was not cross-examined by respondent side. 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. But despite opportunity given, no arguments addressed by respondent side. In fact, as per record, after appearing initially, in 2020, respondent side stopped appearing and participating in the present proceedings. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287 ], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. 13. In the present case, police after investigation had MACT No. 165/2020 Hamid Khan v. Yamin Page No 4 of 19 BK filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 14. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 19. Further it can be noted that the heads under which MACT No. 165/2020 Hamid Khan v. Yamin Page No 6 of 19 BK compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) 19.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 19.7. 23. Interest is compensation for forbearance or detention of money and that interest being awarded to a party only for being kept out of the money which ought to have been paid to him. 24. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 25. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs.65,000/- with simple interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till its actual realization. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, MACT No. 165/2020 Hamid Khan v. Yamin Page No 14 of 19 BK the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having Master Hamid Khan(Minor) vs Yamin S/O Sh.
